objects.original: Euclidean objective f, its actual gradient trajectory, and attained minimizer x_star with value f_star.
objects.reconstructed: Objective f, actual Riesz gradient, supplied trajectory X, and globally minimizing point z with value f(z).
objects.evidence: The complete real inner-product structure identifies the gradient with the Frechet derivative by the Riesz map. IsMinOn f univ z states global minimality; no surrogate gradient or freely chosen energy replaces f.

domains.original: R^d and a forward trajectory indexed by nonnegative real time.
domains.reconstructed: Any complete real inner-product space; X is defined on R but constrained only on [0,T], with right derivatives on [0,T).
domains.evidence: This is a valid Hilbert-space and finite-horizon generalization, not literal domain equivalence. Only the time interval is required compact: the proof takes the minimum of a continuous real-valued function on [0,T], never assumes compact bounded subsets of E. Negative-time values and values beyond T are unused.

quantifiers.original: Every admissible objective and supplied flow, at positive elapsed time, with a minimum over the whole elapsed interval.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universal f, X, z, T subject to the hypotheses; existential s in [0,T] satisfying IsMinOn and the rate.
quantifiers.evidence: The existential s realizes the source minimum and is allowed to depend on the curve and T. The witness minimizes over every u in [0,T], not just a finite sample or terminal time. Universal z is harmless because every global minimizer has the same value.

assumptions.original: Standing C2 regularity and attained minimum; supplied gradient ODE; no convexity or PL condition.
assumptions.reconstructed: C1 Frechet regularity; global minimizing z; T>0; continuous X on [0,T] with the actual right-gradient ODE on [0,T).
assumptions.evidence: C1 replaces C2 and finite-horizon right-derivative data replace a full forward flow. These are mathematically sufficient: C1 gives continuous gradient, the chain rule gives right energy derivative minus gradient norm squared, and scalar right-slope comparison closes the estimate. Explicit continuity and global minimality do not add restrictions to the source setting. No flow existence or uniqueness is proved.

conclusion.original: Corollary 2.8 bounds the minimum gradient norm by sqrt((f(x_0)-f_star)/t).
conclusion.reconstructed: A minimizing time s exists and its gradient norm is at most sqrt((f(X(0))-f(z))/T).
conclusion.evidence: The exact square-root bound and attained minimum are retained. Continuity of gradient composed with X and nonempty compact [0,T] establish attainment. The preceding source average inequality is proof context, not an additional claimed exported conclusion; no terminal-time rate is asserted.

scopes.original: Section 2 supplies forward-time conventions; the normalized expression requires positive elapsed time.
scopes.reconstructed: Strict T>0, including both endpoints in the minimizing interval; the ODE is required before T only.
scopes.evidence: The pinned Corollary 2.8 does not state a separate explicit t>0 clause, while its denominator t rules out a finite real interpretation at zero. The packet correctly restricts its claimed finite quotient to positive time. This review does not certify the formula at t=0, nor propose any zero-time repair. No derivative at T is needed by the checked right-slope comparison.

constant_dependencies.original: Unit coefficient, initial objective gap and elapsed time only.

constant_dependencies.evidence: K=0 and forcing minus the attained minimum squared yield T*m^2 <= initial gap. Division by T>0 and the nonnegative square root preserve coefficient one. There are no dimension, smoothness, convexity, PL, or hidden comparison constants.
